cards.answer: Miss Fortune is a marksman and mage who deals bonus physical damage when switching attack targets. She can slow enemies in an area and channel a cone of bullets for heavy damage.
cards.counterplay: Avoid standing behind her targets or grouping inside her bullet cone.

cards.answer: Basic attacks against a new eligible target deal bonus physical damage. Switching targets lets Love Tap trigger again.
cards.counterplay: Expect extra damage when she switches her attacks onto you.

citations.quote: Miss Fortune deals bonus physical damage whenever she basic attacks a new target.

facts.claim: Basic attacks against a new eligible target deal bonus physical damage.

citations.quote: Miss Fortune's basic attacks apply a mark that expires when attacking a new enemy. If the enemy was unmarked, this also deals bonus physical damage.

facts.claim: Switching targets lets Love Tap trigger again.

passive_visual.description: The mark follows her latest attack target and changes when she attacks a different enemy.

cards.priority_reason: Switching targets increases her attack damage and helps restore Strut.
uncertainties: The visible mark cue remains a tentative proposal from the supplied official-clip frames, not current-client or skin-specific verification. Its description makes no appearance or placement claim.

Advanced exceptions omitted from beginner text: reduced bonus damage against minions, no trigger against buildings, primary-target-only interaction with Runaan's Hurricane, and life steal application.

cards.answer: Double Up fires a targeted shot that deals physical damage and can bounce to another enemy behind the first. Both hits can apply Love Tap.
cards.counterplay: Avoid standing directly behind an enemy she can shoot.

citations.quote: Miss Fortune fires a bullet at an enemy, damaging them and a target behind them.
Miss Fortune fires a shot at the target enemy that deals physical damage, which then bounces to hit another enemy behind them.

facts.claim: Double Up fires a targeted shot that deals physical damage and can bounce to another enemy behind the first.

citations.quote: Both strikes can also apply Love Tap.

facts.claim: Both hits can apply Love Tap.

cards.priority_reason: The bounce threatens enemies standing behind other units.
uncertainties: The bounce requires an eligible secondary target. It can critically strike and is guaranteed to do so when Double Up kills the primary target.
Advanced targeting priorities, on-attack and on-hit interactions, spell shields, attack-range adjustments and cast cancellation are omitted from beginner text.

cards.answer: Strut builds movement speed in two stages after avoiding damage other than recurring damage over time. Activating it instantly grants the higher movement speed bonus and temporarily boosts attack speed. Love Tap triggers reduce Strut's remaining cooldown.
cards.counterplay: Deal direct damage to disrupt her passive movement speed, and respect her attack-speed boost.

citations.quote: Miss Fortune gains bonus movement speed after 4 seconds without taking non- periodic damage. This bonus is increased after another 3 seconds, and is granted instantly whenever Strut is cast.

facts.claim: Strut builds movement speed in two stages after avoiding damage other than recurring damage over time.

citations.quote: This bonus is increased after another few seconds, and is granted instantly whenever Strut is cast.
This ability can be activated to grant bonus Attack Speed for a short duration.

facts.claim: Activating it instantly grants the higher movement speed bonus and temporarily boosts attack speed.

citations.quote: While it's on cooldown, Love Taps reduce the remaining cooldown of Strut.
Marking a new target with Love Tap reduces Strut's current cooldown by 2 seconds.

facts.claim: Love Tap triggers reduce Strut's remaining cooldown.

cards.priority_reason: Explains her movement, attack-speed boost and target-switching synergy.
uncertainties: Riot summarizes the passive condition as not being attacked; Wiki specifies non-periodic damage. The answer explains this as damage other than recurring damage over time.
Wiki states that zero-damage instances do not remove the movement speed bonus; counterplay assumes damage is actually dealt.

cards.answer: Make It Rain creates a temporary bullet storm at a chosen location, repeatedly dealing magic damage and slowing enemies inside. It also grants sight of the area.
cards.counterplay: Leave the bullet storm to avoid further damage and slowing.

cards.answer: Bullet Time channels repeated waves of bullets into a cone in front of Miss Fortune, dealing physical damage. Each wave can critically strike.
cards.counterplay: Move out of the cone quickly, or interrupt her channel with an effect that prevents her from casting abilities.

Each target can take damage from only one projectile per wave. Spell shields do not block the barrage; projectile blocking and channel interruption are distinct interactions.
